questions.corrige_markdown: A **computer network** is a collection of two or more computers and other devices (printers, servers, phones...) that are **connected together**, by cables or by wireless links, so that they can **communicate and share resources** (data, files, programs, hardware such as printers, and an Internet connection).

questions.enonce_markdown: State and explain THREE advantages and TWO disadvantages of using Computer Networks.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Advantages (three of the following):**

1. **Resource sharing.** Expensive hardware (printers, scanners, a large disk) and software can be shared by all users, which reduces cost.
2. **Communication and collaboration.** Users can exchange messages (e-mail, chat) and work on the same files from different places, which saves time.
3. **Centralised data and backup.** Files stored on a server are available to every authorised user, are always up to date and are backed up in a single place; security (user accounts, permissions) is managed centrally.
4. Software can be installed, licensed and updated once for the whole network.

**Disadvantages (two of the following):**

1. **Security risks.** Many users and connections make unauthorised access, hacking and the spread of viruses and malware easier, so firewalls, passwords and anti-virus software are needed.
2. **Cost of installation and maintenance.** Cables, switches, servers and a technician are costly, and the network must be maintained.
3. **Dependence on the network.** If the server or a main link fails, many users cannot work, and heavy traffic can slow the network down.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new company has been established. It bought some new premises which consist of a number of buildings on a single site. It decided that all of the computer workstations in the different buildings need to be networked. The company's technical services are considering ways in which the network might be set up.

One option considered is to use cabling for the network and to install it themselves.

Name the three types of cabling that they might consider.
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Twisted pair** cable (unshielded UTP or shielded STP, for example Cat 5e / Cat 6 Ethernet cable).
2. **Coaxial** cable.
3. **Fibre optic** cable.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new company has been established. It bought some new premises which consist of a number of buildings on a single site. It decided that all of the computer workstations in the different buildings need to be networked.

One option considered is to use cabling for the network and to install it themselves.

Explain two factors, other than cost, that they need to consider when choosing suitable cabling.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two of the following, each with its explanation:

1. **Bandwidth (data transfer rate).** The cable must carry the amount of traffic expected: fibre optic carries far more data per second than coaxial or twisted pair, which matters for the links between buildings where the traffic of many workstations is combined.
2. **Maximum cable length / signal attenuation.** Signals weaken with distance: twisted pair is limited to about 100 m per segment, whereas fibre optic can run for kilometres. Because the workstations are in different buildings, the distance between them decides which cable can be used without repeaters.
3. **Interference and security.** Electromagnetic interference from motors or power lines corrupts signals in copper cables; fibre is immune to it and is also very hard to tap.
4. **Ease of installation and flexibility.** Twisted pair is cheap to handle and flexible; fibre needs special tools and skills for splicing and connectors, and outdoor links between buildings need protected (armoured or buried) cable.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new company has been established. It bought some new premises which consist of a number of buildings on a single site. It decided that all of the computer workstations in the different buildings need to be networked.

Another option considered is to use wireless technology for at least part of the network.

Explain one type of wireless network that might be suitable for wireless networking.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN, Wi-Fi)** is suitable. Wireless access points (wireless routers) are connected to the wired network and broadcast radio signals (IEEE 802.11 standards, in the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands). Each workstation or laptop has a wireless network adapter and connects to the nearest access point using a network name (SSID) and a security key (WPA2 / WPA3). Several access points can be placed in the different buildings of the site so that the whole site is covered, and users can move between them while staying connected.

(Another acceptable answer: a point-to-point wireless bridge or microwave link between two buildings.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new company has been established. It bought some new premises which consist of a number of buildings on a single site. It decided that all of the computer workstations in the different buildings need to be networked.

Another option considered is to use wireless technology for at least part of the network.

Identify one advantage, other than cost, of using wireless rather than cable networking.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Mobility and flexibility**: users can connect and move around the site with laptops or phones, and workstations can be added or moved without installing new cables or drilling through walls (and no cable has to be run between buildings). (Another acceptable answer: easy to extend the network.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A new company has been established. It bought some new premises which consist of a number of buildings on a single site. It decided that all of the computer workstations in the different buildings need to be networked.

Another option considered is to use wireless technology for at least part of the network.

Identify one disadvantage (other than cost) of using wireless rather than cable networking.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Lower security**: radio signals can be intercepted by anyone within range, so the network must be encrypted (WPA2 / WPA3) and protected by a password. (Other acceptable answers: slower and less stable than cable, because the signal is weakened by walls and distance and suffers interference from other devices; a limited range.)
